blocks.eyebrow: Chapter 2 - Making a ledger out of it
blocks.heading: Proving membership
text: Nora's phone tells her the 0.05 has arrived. It is holding none of the chain - hundreds of gigabytes it has no room for.

blocks.heading: The naive version does not fit
text: To confirm Caleb's payment is in a block, she could download the block and look. That is megabytes for one line of interest.
The alternative is not to compress the block. It is to build it so that inclusion can be proved without it.

blocks.heading: Pair, hash, repeat
text: Hash the transaction ids in pairs, then hash those in pairs, until one hash remains. That is the Merkle root.

blocks.alt: A Merkle tree over eight transactions; the three sibling hashes forming the proof are highlighted and numbered, the recomputed path is outlined
blocks.caption: Orange is what the proof carries. Outlined is what Nora's phone works out for itself.

blocks.heading: What she is actually sent
text: Her own transaction, three sibling hashes, and the block header. She hashes her way up and compares the result to the root in the header.
If they match, that transaction is in that block. Nothing else needed to be downloaded.

blocks.heading: It scales the good way
text: Every doubling of the block adds exactly one hash to the proof.

blocks.caption: A full block costs her twelve hashes. That is the whole reason phones can do this.

blocks.question: The proof is just hashes, and whoever sent it chose them. Why can a lying node not invent a set that reaches the right root?
answer: Because reaching a chosen root means finding inputs that hash to a fixed value - a second pre-image, then a collision at the level above it.
That is $2^{128}$ work at best. The root in the header was fixed before the proof was requested, and nothing can be fitted to it afterwards.

text: That the transaction is _in a block_. Not that the block is on the winning chain. Not that the transaction was valid - her phone never checked a signature or an input.
A light client trusts miners for validity and the header chain for ordering. It verifies membership, and outsources everything else.

blocks.heading: The bug in the odd case
text: When a level has an odd number of nodes, bitcoin duplicates the last one to make a pair.
So a tree over three transactions and a tree over the same three with the last repeated produce **the same root**.

CVE-2012-2459: take a valid block, duplicate transactions inside it to reach an identical root, and relay that. Nodes checking the root would accept the structure, fail the duplicate-spend check, and mark the **original** block invalid.
A denial of service against a perfectly good block, built out of one convenience in the tree construction.

blocks.heading: How her phone gets the proof
text: Early light wallets sent a filter describing the addresses they cared about, which told the node exactly who they were.
BIP-158 inverts it: the node publishes one filter per block, the phone downloads it and checks locally. The question never leaves the device.

blocks.heading: One sentence worth keeping
text: A Merkle proof buys you membership in logarithmic space, and buys you nothing else at all.
Everything her phone checked hangs off one 32-byte field in a header. Next: the other 48 bytes.
